Radiology Report
Date: 09/06/2026
Patient: Cary Hintz, 68-year-old male

MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/06/2026: acute osteoporotic L2 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging. Interval increase in L2 vertebral body height loss compared with radiographs from 07/18/2026. Focal kyphotic deformity at L2 measuring 18 degrees.

Impression:
Acute osteoporotic compression fracture of the L2 vertebral body with bone marrow edema. There is an interval increase in vertebral body height loss compared with prior radiographs. A focal kyphotic deformity at L2 measuring 18 degrees is present.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is recommended. Consider follow-up imaging to assess fracture progression and spinal alignment.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/09/2026
Patient: Cary Hintz, 68-year-old male

History of Present Illness:
Back pain began 07/16/2026 after lifting a laundry basket, 8 weeks before this visit. Pain NRS 5/10 despite 7 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and tramadol, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture. Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Clinical Course:
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program.

Plan:
Continue current conservative management. Monitor pain and function. Follow up after DEXA results and osteoporosis program progress. Consider interventional options if pain worsens or function declines.
